title: Rust: Custom Error Types
description: Define custom error types with the Error trait for better error handling.

steps.title: Define a Custom Error Enum
steps.description: Define an enum `AppError` with variants `NotFound`, `InvalidInput`, and `PermissionDenied`. Implement `Display` and `Debug` for it. Print each variant.

verification.failureMessage: Define AppError and print each variant.

steps.title: Custom Error in Result
steps.description: Write a function `validate_age(age: i32) -> Result<i32, AppError>` that returns `InvalidInput` if age < 0 or age > 150, else `Ok(age)`. Test with 25, -5, and 200.
hints: Use match to handle the Result.
Return the result and print appropriate messages.

steps.title: Implement Error Trait
steps.description: Implement `std::error::Error` for your `AppError` type (needed for `?` operator compatibility). Demonstrate using it with the `?` operator in a function.
hints: `impl std::error::Error for AppError {}` — the std::error::Error trait for simple enums.
This enables `?` in functions returning `Result<_, AppError>`.

verification.failureMessage: Use the ? operator with AppError and print results.

steps.title: Wrapping External Errors
steps.description: Extend `AppError` with a `ParseError(String)` variant that wraps parsing errors. Write a function `parse_config(s: &str) -> Result<i32, AppError>` that parses an i32.
hints: This pattern wraps external errors in your custom type.

verification.failureMessage: Parse '42' successfully and show error for 'abc'.

steps.title: Multi-Level Error Propagation
steps.description: Write nested functions: `read_config()`, `parse_config()`, `validate_config()` that each return `Result<_, AppError>` and use `?` to propagate errors up. Print the final result or error chain.
hints: The `?` operator propagates through the entire chain.
